column1: # Each vendor's published API price for a model at a faster speed tier, USD per million tokens: the cards a turn
#   served at that speed is priced at. A file of its own beside published-rates.tsv because daemons in the field fetch
#   that file every hour and refuse a header they do not know; this one has its own header and is read from the build.
# speed: fast or ultrafast. A model with no row for a speed has no card at it, and a turn served at that speed is left
#   unpriced, never priced at the standard card. The standard card is published-rates.tsv's row for the same host and
#   model; a speed card is used only beside one.
# These are the short-context cards (input at or under 272K tokens). A request past a model's long-context threshold at
# cache_write is the 30-minute write, as published-rates.tsv's cache_write is for these models.
# OpenAI: developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, the "Fast" and "Ultrafast" tabs, read Nov 16, 2026. Fast was named
#   Priority processing until July 30, 2026. Ultrafast is published for gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.1-sol only. GPT-5.6 Sol's
#   Fast price follows its promotional standard price, which the page says holds until November 30, 2026: re-read it
#   then. The chatgpt.com rows carry the same cards: a plan turn priced here reads as what the same work would cost on
#   the API at the speed it was served at.
